utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Mathias Neuner, Daryl Mundis, and our case manager, Ana Vrljic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances for Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honour. On behalf of Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel, and Alexis Demirdjian, our legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber would like to greet the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in the courtroom. Before we continue hearing the witness, the Chamber would like to point out the following: First of all, with regard to the issue raised by the Defence about the Prosecution's possibility of refreshing the witness's memory by producing a document that wasn't presented as part of its exhibits, yesterday we said that the Prosecution would address this issue. The Chamber is not fully present, and we therefore give the Prosecution 15 days for their oral response to the position expressed by the Defence. Once we have heard what your position is, we will render our oral decision, because the issue was raised before the Chamber orally. So you have 15 days to prepare your response. Secondly, yesterday when hearing a witness, the Prosecution mentioned the situation of the people who were either in the blacksmith's shop or in the Mehurici primary school. And they described these people as prisoners or detainees. Defence counsel objected to this description, saying that the accused weren't charged with illegal detention. As far as this issue is concerned, the Chamber deliberated about the matter yesterday, and we believe that to the extent that the term "prisoner" or "detainee" is a term used in the indictment, the Prosecution is allowed to use this term. But at this point in time, we won't draw any conclusions about the matter. The Defence believes that these people were being protected by the civilian authorities. Since they allege that they were protected, the parties may use the terms they want to describe for the situation these persons were in. But the Chamber will render a final decision about how this situation should be described. I wanted to point this out to you so as to avoid wasting any time on such issues. And my third point is that the Defence filed a written motion that concerned legal issues; in particular, this concerned a request made to us to prohibit the Prosecution to ask questions that had to do with international conflicts. We have been given a written submission, and the Prosecution also needs to provide a written submission. 15 days should be quite sufficient for the Prosecution to respond to the written submission made by the Defence. So there are two pending motions. There's an oral motion, and there is the written submission that was filed with the Registrar. I wanted to point these things out to you. If there are no other issues to raise, we will now continue -- yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps while the witness is being brought into the courtroom, we appreciate the opportunity to respond both to the oral motion of yesterday and to the written motion. We will certainly endeavour to get our responses prepared as quickly as possible, but certainly within the 15-day limit. I rise, Mr. President, simply to ask the Trial Chamber for any guidance that we might get while the motion that was orally made yesterday is pending; that is, what the Trial Chamber's views would be with respect to the use of any such documents that were the subject of the oral motion between now and the time the Trial Chamber has rendered its decision on the issue. If there's any kind of provisional guidance that we might get pending that oral ruling, we would certainly appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, look, if you're asking me this question, that means that you perhaps intend to present other documents in the course of the testimony of future witnesses. We'll discuss this when we have the break, and we will tell you how one should proceed for the following 15 days since we are waiting for your response, unless it is your intention to show the witness who will be in the courtroom in a minute a new document. Mr. Mundis, is this your intention? Do you intend to show this witness a document that hasn't been disclosed to the Defence as part of the Defence's evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: As part of the Prosecution's evidence. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will not be showing this next witness any such documents. We may, however, reserve the right with respect to future witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. After the break, we will inform you of how we should proceed before the decision is rendered, once we have heard what your position is, once you have filed your written response. You can call the witness into the courtroom now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day. Yes, Mr. President, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll continue with your testimony today. The Prosecution told us yesterday that they needed about another 20 minutes. So I will give them the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I stated yesterday that the Defence had used one hour 20 minutes in examination-in-chief, and the Prosecution has calculated and has not used the -- or has not calculated with the time used for the discussion about the document. This time has been subtracted, as a result of which an hour would be in the Prosecution's opinion be available. Is this a suitable way to proceed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. I'll ask the Defence to tell us what they think about this. It took you one hour and 20 minutes for your examination. We wasted a bit of time given the objections that were made. So the Prosecution says they need another hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is in accordance with your decision. We have no objections to raise. But we are doing our best to have a little time or have enough time to conclude our examination with the witness who will be appearing after this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, everyone. We'll try to proceed expeditiously. Let's try to proceed in a manner that will make it possible for the witness to leave when planned. Friday's a holiday, and Monday we won't be working. So the witness will have to stay here for a long time if we can't conclude with the examination as planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karic.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take to you the month of April 1993. On 24 April 1993, the Miletici incident occurred. At that time, where were you located? Were you in Mehurici or were you in another location?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was neither in Mehurici nor in Rudnik. I think I had duties to perform at the lines near Vlasic, on the Vlasic plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did you first come to Mehurici after the Miletici incident?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about the incident in Miletici. I heard about there being a problem there, but I really know nothing about it, and I don't know when I was in Miletici after that event. In fact, I never was in Miletici. I did pass by Miletici when trying to obtain materiel and equipment from the logistics base of the 3rd Corps. But as to the date, as to the time when I passed by Miletici, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Prior to the combat operation on 8 June 1993, were there any independent ABiH forces coming to the area of responsibility of the 306 Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question. This part that concerns the independent ABiH forces, what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let me start again. I was asking you for the period prior to the operation on 8 June 1993. And you testified yesterday that the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was not in the area, or no armed formation of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was in the area prior to 8 of June 1993. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as the organisation of any unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade, no one was there as far as I can remember. Perhaps there were individual members of the 7th Muslim in that area. Perhaps because they weren't able to report to their unit, but yes, what I said is how it was. But I'm quite willing to answer the question, but what I don't understand is, well, how did you put it? Some unofficial, independent army units. There can't be independent, unofficial units which are part of the army. We knew which units were part of the BH Army. That was very clear. And the units that weren't within that structure, they just weren't part of the BH Army. There were such units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to summarise, is it fair to say that your testimony is that maybe individual members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, but no organised formation of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was in the Bila Valley prior to June 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, I can't claim anything for certain. I said that perhaps there were some members of the 7th Muslim Brigade who were on leave at the time, and given the newly developed situation, blockade -- the blockade of the road network, perhaps these people, these men weren't able to return to their units. But I know very little about these things. But that is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to bring the witness Prosecution Exhibit P474, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have the English version of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, if you have a look at this document, it dates from the 22nd of May 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I note that my learned colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Kubura's Defence would like to object to this document being shown to the witness. We have already said that this is a 7th Brigade document. And since Mr. Kubura's Defence will be calling witnesses before this Chamber, only members of the 7th Brigade can talk about such a document. The 306th Brigade isn't mentioned in this document, so there is no reason to show the witness the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What does the Prosecution say to the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I address this issue in the absence of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll be wasting more time now. But Madam Usher, could you escort the witness out of the courtroom. I'll give the floor to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness has yesterday and today stated that there were no armed formations of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the Bila Valley prior to the 8th June offensive. And this document -- or facts deriving, originating from this document show that there were indeed 92 members of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in Mehurici, an area which the witness visited according to his testimony from yesterday. And I just want to show this fact to him. I don't have the witness -- I don't intend that the witness adopts this document or says he has direct knowledge about it. I just want to confront him with the fact that contrary to his testimony, according to this document, there were 92 members, as you can see below under numerical strengths, in the very last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are saying that this document shows that the 7th Brigade was present in Mehurici. On what basis do you make this claim? What allows you to make such a claim in the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The document dates from the 22nd of May 1993. So roughly two weeks before the offensive. And there's another document on the Prosecution's exhibit list which follows up from this document and which then involves the 306 Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just like to say that on page 2, they mention the strength of the 7th Brigade. It doesn't say that there is an organised unit in the area the witness is speaking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Judges believe that in order to test the credibility of a witness, one may produce a document that might contradict the witness's testimony. So you may show the witness this document. Madam Usher, could you bring the witness back into courtroom, please. Yes, Mr. Bourgon. Our decision has been rendered. No more objections. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I take note of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You may go ahead and put this question to the witness in order to test his credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, I mentioned already that the document dates from the 22nd of May 1993, and it mentions the presence of the 1st Battalion, or members of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in certain locations. If you please look at the very last paragraph where it says: "Numerical strengths of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade." Do you find this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you please look under Mehurici --

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Which document are you referring to? Which document refers to Mehurici? It's the second document. It's on page 2. Please be precise when referring to documents. Otherwise we won't be able to follow you. When I asked you a minute ago where this location was referred to, it wasn't on page 1, it was on page 2. So it's best to be precise to avoid any errors. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if you please look at page 2 under the heading "numerical Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond strengths of the 1st Battalion, 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade," do you find Mehurici there? Can you please state so? Do you find Mehurici there?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many soldiers have been on 22nd of May 1993, according to this document, in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, it says that there were 92 soldiers in Mehurici. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I may ask, 92 soldiers, where could they have been located in Mehurici? You testified yesterday there were no barrack in a strict sense. Where could 92 soldiers be located in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll have to ask Mr. Semir Terzic about that. Because I don't know where these soldiers were as an organised whole in the area of Mehurici. And in any case, this document hasn't been signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to bring a new document, Prosecution Exhibit P481.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you please have a look at it, the date of the document is the 27th of May, 1993. So it's five days after the previously shown document. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 of this document mentions the redeployment of 20 soldiers of the 1st Company of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade from the Mehurici sector. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And paragraph 2 of this document mentions that these 20 soldiers from the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade is to be resubordinated. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Resubordinated to the 306 Brigade and to a unit from Radojcici village. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says here. May I comment on this paragraph, please. First of all, I don't know who this document was forwarded to. Did the 306th Brigade receive this document? What sort of a territorial-based unit was there in the village of Radojcici? This concept is not clear to me. A territorially-based unit in the village of Radojcici. This is something I don't understand. As a member of the command of the 306 Mountain Brigade, I have never seen this document, and I don't know whether it was ever forwarded to the 306 Brigade. I don't know if this 1st Company referred to here was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, if I may ask, you mentioned the village of Radojcici. Do you know where the village of Radojcici is located?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I would show you a map, could you indicate where the village of Radojcici is?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the permission of Your Honours, can the witness please be shown this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please point on the ELMO next to you on the village of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Mehurici, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just take a moment to find it. [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please now show the village of Radojcici.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many kilometres away from Guca Gora is the village of Radojcici? What do you estimate?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How many kilometres, you said? Well, two to three I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Two to three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a rough estimate on my part. If you want an exact calculation, I can give you that, too, and have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please take a pen now and encircle the village of Mehurici, or let's start this -- please encircle the village of Radojcici first.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village or where it says Radojcici, the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you please --

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village or the name? Because the village is round here. Do you want me to draw a circle around that, the settlement, the village, or around the name where it says Radojcici?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As you just did, the village itself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you put a 1 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do the same for Mehurici now, please, encircle it and put a 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- just Mehurici, the narrow proper Mehurici proper village, you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mehurici proper, please.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can now turn your attention back to the document, please, the document I showed you before, can I turn your attention back, please. You mentioned -- or it says in the document in paragraph 2 that the company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade is resubordinated to the 306. What does the term "resubordination" mean to you?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, that the company is subordinated to the 306. To be subordinated means that complete control over the unit that is being resubordinated. That's what resubordination means.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 3 of the document, paragraph 3 mentions that logistical supplies shall be secured through the 306 Brigade. As assistant commander for logistics of the 306 Brigade at the time, was -- were you personally - I think you answered it already - or was the person dealing with logistics in Mehurici probably involved in the execution of this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember ever having seen this document as I said. But I personally did not know -- even if it was like this, I didn't know about it. But I don't really believe that the situation was as it is set out here, I really don't. Because not a single unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade relied on the logistics of the 306 Brigade. I can say that with full responsibility. At least as far as matters reached me, the assistant commander for logistics. And I can also claim that this unit -- what does it say here? How is that said? That the members of the 1st Company are resubordinated quite certainly on the terrain of Mehurici. That wasn't done during that period of time. And I say that with full responsibility. I never saw those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned yesterday that at some point in time in May 1993, the brigade command of the 306 was encircled or was in Krpeljici? Do you know where Krpeljici is?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to clarify matters there, too. The complete command of the 306 Brigade wasn't encircled at Krpeljici. Part of the command - that is to say, the commander, the Chief of Staff, the assistant for morale and moral guidance - might have been. But I can show you where the village of Krpeljici is on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please show where the village of Krpeljici is.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now encircle Krpeljici and mark a 3 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How far away from Guca Gora is Krpeljici? Please give an estimate in kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, up to one kilometre, although there's no actual division between the villages, Guca Gora, I mean, and Krpeljici. One follows on from the other. It's linked. And the population is also mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was the reason for parts of the brigade command, 306 Brigade command, to be in Krpeljici at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question because the commander decided where he was going to be and who he was going to be there with at any given point in time and in any given area. I know why they couldn't leave Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond Krpeljici, for instance, but I do not know why the commander went there in the first place. So the commander is the person who decides where he's going to go and who he's going to go there with. He knows the reasons. I can't tell you. I don't know. But I do know why they were not able to leave Krpeljici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did the commander or his direct staff, when did they -- part of his direct staff, when did they go there, to Krpeljici, what date?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I'm sure you have records of that and can find it. As a member of the command, I myself can't remember when that actually took place. But it's common knowledge. It's not a problem to find that piece of data.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you now to Maline on the 8th of June, 1993 -- excuse me, I want to take you to Mehurici on the 8th of June, 1993. You testified you stayed in Mehurici proper on the 8th of June, 1993. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where exactly were you staying that day in Mehurici? At the school?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was staying between the school and the clinic collecting up the motor vehicles because we had to find transport to transport the wounded, carts and whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were there other senior officers present of the 306 Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the command, on that day, there was just Fazlic of the senior officers. But he wasn't there that day, that particular day. While I was there I'm saying. While I was there. I didn't spend the whole day in Mehurici either. So while I was there, he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So while you were there, who was the most senior officer in the time period you were there on the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have been me, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were there any members of the 3rd Corps next to you, or you personally within the 306 were the most senior officer? But were there also any 3rd Corps members on 8th of June in Mehurici? Did you see anybody?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, from the corps, in the afternoon I seem to remember having met Mr. Merdan from the command of the 3rd Corps. I don't know whether he was in the command, but of the senior officers who came to Mehurici in the afternoon, there was Mr. Merdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So until the arrival of Mr. Merdan, you were the most senior officer in rank, and then Mr. Merdan came in the afternoon. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But when we're talking about the most senior rank here, I was assistant commander for logistics, and my assignments were very clear-cut on the basis of the position I occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why -- you met Mr. Merdan when he was arriving in the afternoon? Did you personally meet him?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you talk?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did talk, but I asked him what direction he had come from, and he said he had come from -- I don't remember now. Some direction. He had a sandwich to eat, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At the time you met Mr. Merdan, was the -- were the people from Maline, had they already arrived at the Mehurici school? Or did Mr. Merdan pass by before these people had been -- were arriving?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him on the premises of the forestry department's cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you convey a message to Mr. Merdan about what you learned being there all the time while he was just passing through?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please believe me when I say that I just can't remember details like that. I can't remember everything I said to Mr. Merdan on the occasion. Probably, the information I had received, I told him, but it was information that hadn't been checked out yet, so it was only based on the stories that were going round.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, did Mr. Merdan pass through, or did he intend to stay? Did he mention anything? Did he intend to stay in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I really and honestly don't remember what Mr. Merdan would have had to do after and what he intended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My last question relating to Mr. Merdan would be, do you know where he was coming from?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. As I say, I'm not quite sure, but I seem to remember him having coming from Zenica, or at least from the direction of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: He arrived in the afternoon, in the morning? Any idea what the daylight was?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't be certain what time of day. I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned yesterday that in the course of the 8th of June in Mehurici, you received information that HVO members from Maline, and as you put it, "had been kidnapped by members of the Mujahedin detachment." Do you remember at what point in time on 8th of June you received that information?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What time I received that information?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but perhaps there has been a mistake. Page 19, line 7, it says that the witness said the Mujahedin detachment. As far as I remember, the witness didn't speak about any detachment. All he mentioned was the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have this -- this is actually a cut and paste from the transcript from yesterday, page 62 of the transcript. But I can rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you had any -- at what point in time did you receive any information that possibly members from the Mujahedin had kidnapped, as you put it, HVO members from Maline? At what point of the day did you receive that information?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember the exact time. But upon arrival of those people, escorted by members of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade, perhaps, so after their arrival -- well, that's when I received that piece of information. And it's something that one knows. I think it was before noon. But again, I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I continue to quote you, you said also on page 62 of the transcript, and I quote: "And perhaps" - in addition to the Mujahedin I mean, and I quote: "And perhaps there were some local people accompanying them as well. That's a possibility." Whom do you refer to by "local people"?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean anything. I just said what I had heard from the man who was accompanying them, or rather those members of the 306th Mountain Brigade, the 1st Battalion. So I just said what I had heard from those people, those men. There's nothing for me to think or not think about it. That was information I had received from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, you just testified you heard from those members of the 306 1st Battalion. Do you recall which members did tell you, did provide you with this information?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. I don't remember the name, but that's not a problem either. That's something that one can find out very easily because we know which men accompanied those civilians, the civilians who were brought into Mehurici. That's something that can be easily established.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said "we can find out which men did accompany the civilians." Did you at the time have an idea about the identities of some of these men who were doing the escorting?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After all the time that has gone by, I really can't. I can't be more specific. I would happily do so if I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Once you got this information, were there any discussion among the senior officers in Mehurici about taking measures or about -- to find out Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond the fate of the missing Croat people from Maline? Were there any discussions?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to try and clarify matters in that respect, if I might be allowed to do so. At that point in time, when all this was going on, the conflict was still going on. There was still heavy fighting. And everyone from the brigade command had their assignments and duties. I said yesterday what my duties and assignments were in the area. First of all, I had to see to the wounded and to see that the people who were coming in should be sent their different ways at the request of the commanders and so on. Now, what the talks and discussions were on the issue and who led them, who conducted them, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The ABiH soldiers who had escorted these people to the Mehurici school were probably around the school or in the vicinity. And the Croat civilians who could make it to the school were also - I don't want to say at your disposal, but were also in the school. So wasn't it discussed just to interview the escorters or the civilians being kept at the school to find out what exactly had happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the witness has answered that question at least three times and said everything he knew about the matter. I think that these questions now could be understood as being pressure on the witness or badgering the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Prosecution, the Defence says that you have asked the question. It's asked and answered several times. You've asked him whether there were discussions among the officers about the situation. The witness said he didn't know. And the Defence considers that in repeating your question is a form of badgering the witness. So perhaps you could move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At what time did you leave Mehurici on 8th of June to go to Hum?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On the map next to you, would you be in a position to point out where -- I think you met the 306 Brigade command there. Would you be in a position to point out where you met them?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I met them. Well, it was towards evening in Krpeljici, but very briefly. I met the commander very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't really say it was a meeting. It was just a brief encounter and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand. But do you recall anybody being present at that meeting? Who was present?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. But I know that -- well, I don't really know who was there. I know that I met the commander of the 306th Mountain Brigade, Mr. Sipic, for a very brief moment. He had his tasks and job to do. I had my assignments, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday there was also a security organ there. Do you remember the name of the security organ?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ was not in Krpeljici. The security organ was at Rudnik, according to my information, according to what I know. Now, who was there and whether anybody was there from the brigade command of the security organs, I don't know. But you have to realise that in the battalion you have people who dealt in affairs of security, intelligence, logistics, and so on and so forth. I have the feeling that you might not have realised that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned yesterday that at this meeting it was mentioned by the security organ, and I quote: "It was possible that a crime was committed there." I'm referring to the disappearance of the Croat people from Maline.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't that day, the 8th of June. At the meeting of the brigade command, which was held after -- three or four days, or two or three or four days later, I don't know the exact date, that's when I received official information from the first time or first heard about this information from the representatives of the security organs about the issue. So that was the first official information as a member of the command that I received and learned, that it was possible that what had happened there had actually happened. What they say happened there actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying this. You said three or four days later. Do you recall the location of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact place where the meeting was held. But it has all been recorded in our documents, so...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at the end of this meeting where you first -- or the command of the 306th first learned that possibly a crime was committed, was there any conclusion taken at the end of the meeting in terms of measures, conclusion to find out what was really happening, whether the possibility of a crime was, in fact, a reality?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command does not bring in conclusions. The command is an organ with a number of component parts. It has the security section, the operations section, logistics, moral guidance, and so on. And in principle, each of those organs are given assignments after the reports have come in. The commander issues assignments at the proposal of his assistants. You keep wanting to try and extract information from me, but you have to realise that at that point in time my task was to supply a front line with the logistics necessary, a front line that was even bigger than the front line towards the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor. So you had to provide logistics for this whole area which was a large area, a large front. But what I can tell you is about my own situation. Of course, each department had their own problems. The moral guidance man had his problems, the operations man had his problems and so on. I had to find -- or they would say -- somebody would say I have to find men to dig trenches, for example, just to paint a picture of what was going on for you. But what I do remember is this: I know that the -- that what was sort of decided was to carry on trying to find out what actually happened there because we were responsible men. So I suppose that our organs and departments did take certain steps to throw as much light on the matter as possible within the frameworks of our competencies, to find out what actually happened in Maline.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether anybody was tasked with going after this incident as a result of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A while ago, I said brigades have organs whose duty it is to take such measures. And I believe that the people responsible did what they could to the extent it was possible. You know how these things work. You have the commander and you have the assistant commander, and this is how one proceeds.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few more questions. Please, just answer this question with yes or no. Were you present when Guca Gora, when the ABiH took Guca Gora following the meeting in the night of the 8th of June in Krpeljici? Were you personally present?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question. The witness never said that there was a meeting on the 8th of June in Krpeljici. He said that he briefly met the commander, and then went to perform other duties elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is exactly why I'm asking the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You went - you testified yesterday - to perform other duties. So with this -- with the question I just put to you, I want to find out whether you were in Guca Gora or whether you were performing your duties somewhere else? Maybe a few kilometres away from Guca Gora? Were you present in Guca Gora the next day, when the ABiH took Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following day, I think I passed through Guca Gora, but I wasn't there on the day that the army took Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did the army take Guca Gora, the ABiH Army?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I have, was it on the 8th or the 9th Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond of June, I don't know. I don't remember. When the population of Guca Gora evacuated with the help of UNPROFOR, et cetera, that's when this occurred. I think it was on the 8th or on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said the following day you passed through Guca Gora. Is this the 9th of June? Just to clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. Perhaps it was the 9th. Perhaps it was the 10th. I don't know. But on the following day when it was possible to pass through Guca Gora, I passed through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which ABiH units did you see in Guca Gora when you passed through on the 9th or the 10th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only noticed members of the military police in Guca Gora, MPs who were providing security for the monastery in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You returned in 1994 the Guca Gora monastery. At the time you returned, you handed over the Guca Gora monastery, were all the books from the library -- were all the books still left in the library of the Guca Gora monastery?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may provide you with a lengthy answer with regard to the library in the monastery in Guca Gora, may I? Thank you. When I became commander of the 306th Mountain Brigade, I didn't move into the Guca Gora monastery immediately. Upon moving into the monastery, we established a library. We formed a library out of the books that had remained there. They were all put in order. And during the handover, this library wasn't handed over to the clergy representatives. It was packed and handed over to the archives. And the civilian authorities returned what had remained of the library to the monastery in Guca Gora. I don't know exactly when this was done. I don't know the exact year. But the books that remained were returned to the monastery in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said when you -- being commander of the 306, saw the books for the first time in the library. What was your impression? Was the library complete by then, or were some books missing?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you what my personal impression was. I don't know what sort of books were contained in the library before I moved into the monastery in Guca Gora. The books weren't in the condition they should have been in, but of the books remaining there, the documents, et cetera, from the Vatican, from the local church, et cetera, well, we put all these books and documents into order. When we left the monastery, we packed the books. They were then transferred to the archives of Central Bosnia. They were transferred from the command of the 306th in the primary school to the Central Bosnian archives. And then the books from returned from the archives in Central Bosnia to the monastery, at least the books that we had found in the library were returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At least the books you found. Can you maybe try to give a quantity from your impression what you saw of books being present, books being not present?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I really wouldn't want to waste time on objections, but I would be grateful if my learned colleague could tell us what the purpose of these questions is since the count in the indictment concerns the destruction of the monastery. And I don't see the purpose of asking questions about the library since we have had evidence about this matter. We have been told about what was taken away before the conflict and about other items. But given the counts in the indictment, I don't know whether it's necessary to spend so much time on this issue. Could my learned colleague please explain the purpose of these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Defence counsel has pointed out that the count in the indictment concerns destruction of the monastery, and Defence counsel is surprised by the fact that you're asking this witness questions about the library and the books contained in the library. But I have found out from the witness that he says that he took books from the library, the books were packed and transferred to the Central Bosnian archives. Subsequently, the books were returned to the monastery. This is the first time we have heard about this. What would the Prosecution like to say in response to the objection raised by the Defence concerning the books? Because apparently these books were not destroyed. I'm listening to what you have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: From the books which were found, certainly these books were not destroyed. But I understood also that some books were missing for whatever reason, and these books, since as the witness also pointed out, they came partially from the Vatican and so on, they might form part of the cultural heritage of the Croat people. But the Prosecution is prepared to move on to its last question relating to Mujahedin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'll ask the witness a question. It will save time. Sir, it seems that some books allegedly disappeared. Could you explain how these books disappeared since these books were part of a people's cultural heritage. When you returned these books, it appears - and I stress "appears" - that some books were missing. Could you answer this question. This is the purpose of the question put to you by the Prosecution, but it would be good to clarify the matter. What would you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was telling you about what I was aware of. But if some of the books were missing, well, that was because the people who went there and didn't know the value of these books. They didn't know what they represented. But when we moved into the monastery with the commander, I know we put these books into order while the command was in the monastery. These books were available to everyone for their consultation, not to take away with them. When the command left, we packed them and took them to a new command place. They were then transferred from the Central Bosnian archives, and the books were subsequently returned to the monastery. As to how many books were destroyed, as to which books were destroyed, I don't know. If that was the case, if this actually did happen, then naturally this is not something that people who were responsible for these books or who were concerned with these books would accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, my last question relates to the Mujahedin. During the war, you pursued a double career. You were a military officer, and you were a politician in the RBiH parliament. The presence of such foreigners in Bosnia had a military and a political aspect to it. During formal or informal sessions of the RBiH parliament, was there ever mention made of the presence of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I don't believe so, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's almost time for our break. It's 10.27. We'll resume at about five minutes to 11.00 for additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give the floor to the Defence now for their additional questions. But before I do so, I would like to point something out. We said that we would render a decision on documents that might be tendered. As far as this issue is concerned, the Trial Chamber has taken note of the request made by the Defence, and the Trial Chamber, when complete, will be rendering a decision. The Trial Chamber distinguishes between two categories of documents. The first category concerns documents that the Prosecution had in its possession, but did not disclose to the Defence before the trial and as part of the evidence presented. The second category of documents concerns documents that the Prosecution obtained after the presentation of its case. The Trial Chamber, on a provisional basis, and before hearing the Prosecution's position expressed orally, hereby decides that when a witness is being heard, only documents from the second category can be presented. That is to say, only documents can be presented that have been obtained after the presentation of the Prosecution's case. In such a case, the Prosecution, before presenting such a document, should inform the Trial Chamber of the following: Firstly, of the source of the document; secondly, of the date on which it obtained the document; thirdly, of the circumstances in which the Prosecution obtained the document. The Trial Chamber also suggests to the Prosecution that they inform us when making their oral submissions in 15 days' time of the general circumstances concerning the Prosecution's knowledge of the documents that they had or obtained after the presentation of its case. I invite the Prosecution to reread this oral decision we have just rendered and which will be in force until our final decision is rendered. This is a decision we will render after we have heard what your position is. And secondly, as I said at the beginning of the hearing - I'll say it again to make it clear - the Chamber authorises both parties to use the terms they want to use to describe the status of the people who were guarded or who had voluntarily gathered in certain locations. If the Prosecution wants to say that they were prisoners, they may. If the Defence wants to say that they were free, they may do so. The parties may use the terms that they deem appropriate. And naturally, given the fact that the parties may use the terms they deem appropriate, they may ask any questions about the people who were detained or who were free. Naturally, the Trial Chamber is always in control of the questions put to witnesses. I wanted to mention all these items to make everything clear. But you may reread the transcript so that you are sure of what has been said. Without wasting more time, I'll give you the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Karic.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the Prosecution has not yet said what they will be doing with the part of the map that they have before you, I would like to ask you to have another look at that map, and under number 2, you marked Mehurici proper. Could you now please encircle on the same map the Mehurici sector, including all the villages and hamlets that are part of that sector.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Mehurici local commune? Or the sector?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what one would consider to be the sector of Mehurici, the local commune, the villages, and the hamlets that were part of that place. As far as I have understood you, you have marked the centre of Mehurici here.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer since he wasn't speaking to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that with an interrupted line so that we can be sure of whether -- the first part of your answer wasn't interpreted. The witness said, "I'm not sure whether Podstinje is part of the Mehurici or Guca Gora local commune. Perhaps it's part of both."

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local commune of Maline.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the local commune of Maline. And as a result, he marked that area with a dotted line. Can you finish doing what you were doing, please.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the situation was. I think that was the local commune of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the central area with a number 4, the area you have just indicated.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, I would like to point out that the witness has outlined the area of the sector, or rather of the Mehurici local commune. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we now take a look at Prosecution Exhibit P481 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by my learned colleague, you said you never saw the document before and then went on to give your explanations. I'd just like to ask you something with respect to point 3. Mr. Karic, if logistics supplies of any unit were to be secured through the 306th Brigade, were you the organ who would conduct the logistical supply issue, or would that be somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the logistics supplies of a military unit had to be secured through the 306th Brigade, would you be the assistant commander who would yourself see to those supplies being secured?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under normal conditions, the functioning of the brigade and its command, I would have to know about activities of this kind. If I had the logistics of a battalion in a certain area, I was able to issue instructions according to the logistics of that battalion with agreement from the battalion commander to secure logistics supplies in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be sufficient. Tell me now, please, did you ever receive an order to supply any company at all or any individuals from the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And that was impossible, if we take a look --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Now, take a look at the document again, please. The document isn't signed.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I'd like to ask you something else about it. You were a military man yourself. Due to forces of circumstance, you also hold a rank. Was it at all possible for the commander of a battalion to resubordinate its men, its unit to another brigade to which it does not belong? Is that possible? Is it possible for a lower ranking officer to resubordinate to another brigade his own men?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Karic, take a look at the first sentence of this order. You've already given some explanations and said that you don't know whether somebody was there or not. But if this order were correct, would it specify the area in which those 20 soldiers could find themselves possibly in some eventuality?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say? Was it specified? Well, it says: "From the Mehurici sector." It says: "From the Mehurici sector to Radojcici village in order to," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, the Mehurici sector, is that what you drew a moment ago on the map for me?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Mehurici sector is even larger, but generally speaking they are the villages incorporated by the Mehurici local commune. Might I be allowed to give another explanation. I do apologise. But may I? Some people consider the Mehurici sector to be much broader, and the Mehurici sector could also incorporate the Dug, Visnje, Vobuka [phoen], Bukovica local communes and even Zabrdje because some people consider that to come under the Mehurici sector. But I limited myself just to the local commune of Mehurici itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, the Mehurici sector, did it look like you have encircled on the map, or was it as other people considered it a much broader region, a much broader sector than the actual place called Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Mehurici sector is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Might the witness now be shown another document, P474.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Once again, would you take a look at page 2 of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they do not have page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom, what does it say? Can you tell me what it says before the names in the document are enumerated. What does it say above that?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "1/7 of the Muslim Mountain Brigade." Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see anywhere on that piece of paper the time when these numbers for the brigade are referring to? The four -- the battalion, the strength. Does this document indicate the time at which these men were in that region, that area?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the time anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I have just one more question for you, Mr. Karic: In response to a question from my learned colleague as to why the commander found himself in Krpeljici, your answer was to say that the commander knows the reasons why he happened to be in Krpeljici. But in continuation on two occasions you tried to say "but I know the reasons why he was not able to leave Krpeljici." Would you tell us now what those reasons were. Why couldn't the commander, members of the command leave Krpeljici and go to the command post? Why was that?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, or rather as far as I remember, the rest of the command from Rudnik and from Mehurici, they had been scattered as I described yesterday when the blockades were set up by the HVO. We insisted that the commander should leave Krpeljici with the help of UNPROFOR. However, that was not enabled them. The HVO did not allow our commander to leave Krpeljici even with UNPROFOR, to pass by their checkpoints and barricades. So Krpeljici, not only the commander and the command, the entire settlement was under a complete siege, a complete encirclement, not with the checkpoints but with the front line going right the way round it and the front line was manned by the HVO members. It was a fortified area, trenches, communicating trenches right the way round the village with members of the HVO and manned by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We have no further questions for this witness. We do wish to note, however, that there have been two documents allegedly from the 7th Brigade shown to this witness. And although the witness was able to say that he saw them as somewhat unusual documents, he wasn't able to give any more information about those particular documents. We are of the view that it will be much more efficient if those documents can be shown to members of the 7th Brigade who may be in a position to explain those documents. And hence, we're not going to ask this witness any further questions about them, but we will certainly return to that matter in order to address any questions that may be outstanding on these documents. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. I have a few questions myself, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We learned something we didn't know before, and that is that you were a deputy, you were elected as a parliamentary deputy and that you were at the assembly meetings where your other colleague deputies were. Having been elected, you ought to know about the political action waged by the state at the time, by the state leadership, and I'd like to ask you whether as a military man or as a deputy at your level, did you have any knowledge of a decree, of a law that was passed by the President, Mr. Izetbegovic, President Izetbegovic, with regard to service in the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina? And that bill, decree, law in actual fact was dated the 1st of August, 1992. Do you know -- are you familiar with the text of the decree concerning the army in general terms, either as a parliamentarian yourself or as an officer, as a military man?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that period, the presidency, because the parliament of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina couldn't function normally, very often it had to take decisions having the force of law. So could you tell us -- tell me what decree that actually was, what the name of the title of the decree and law was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is P243, Exhibit P243, Mr. Registrar. We'll show you the decree law in your own language.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have enough time to read through all of this, but what I can tell you is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you look at Article 31, please. It says in Article 31 that somebody who is not a citizen of the republic can be recruited into the army. Now, my question to you is this: To your knowledge, foreigners who were not citizens, did not have citizenship of your republican state, could they have been recruited into the army, since according to this article that was allowed?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the decree laws of the presidency are concerned, I know that we as parliamentarians and deputies confirmed most of the decrees passed by the presidency at the period of time when regular parliament could be convened. I don't remember exactly when that period was. You can check it out. It's not difficult to find out what period that applied to. But as far as I know, and according to my information, in the area I was in, I don't know that there were any foreigners who were members of the Bosnia-Herzegovinian Army. At least, there were none like that in the 306th Mountain Brigade. I'm certain of that. So that's what I can tell you. I am qualified to speak about the 306th Mountain Brigade, and I say with absolute certainty that there were no foreigners like that in the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll move on to another subject. You said to us on page 54, line 8, that members of the army, that the Mujahedin, in fact, married young girls from the Mehurici region, local young girls. Do you know the name of some young girl or their family names who married Mujahedin? Because when you said that, you were referring to specific cases, were you? Or were you referring to rumours and stories that were going round to that effect that you could have heard here and there? Or do you have personal knowledge of specific cases of marriages between young girls and the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to that problem, I spoke generally -- in general terms yesterday. I know that for most of us, domiciles, locals, this was a very frustrating situation, that very young girls were marrying those foreigners. That's what I know. In general terms, that was the general attitude of the locals. And next, you should understand that it wasn't only the young girls who were local to the area of Mehurici. The area was saturated with refugees and displaced persons, so it wasn't only local young girls from Mehurici who married those guys, those young men, foreigners. So it would be difficult for me to give a name. But people know about it. And if the Court is interested, it would be easy to check out which girls from the area, which local girls married Mujahedin and left to take up their life with them. It's no problem to check it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. But you can't give us a concrete name or case. And to move on to another area: On page 46, line 14 and 49, line 10, you said at a given point, there was the presence of the Croatian Army in the region. So I'm asking you now, what allowed you to say -- what led you to say that the Croatian Army was present in the region? I'm not speaking about the HVO. You mentioned the HV, the Croatian Army at one point. So as a military man yourself, how did you draw that conclusion? Was it something that you saw personally, that you were told about? You received reports about, or were there just rumours going round the parliament and the deputies? Could you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember, I said yesterday, at least at one point in response to a question asked, that in passing through the checkpoints I saw - that's what I saw myself - I saw signs and insignia on people manning those checkpoints, that they had HVO and HOS insignia. And for us, the black shirts were the most dangerous. They didn't have any insignia on themselves. But they had insignia of the HV, with the HV coat of arms. So there was HV, HVO, the HOS, and the black shirts without any insignia whatsoever. Those were the four different categories, and we referred to them that way. We called them black shirts, this fourth group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much for giving me that explanation. And now my last question and area, you were in the 306th Brigade yourself. You were in charge of logistics. If I understand what logistics means, it means that you had the responsibility and task of providing supplies such as food, materiel and equipment. That is what comes under the term "logistics." Is that right? Is that what you were authorised to do? Is that what logistics meant? Did it incorporate those things?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, starting out from that assumption, the school of Mehurici, was it occupied by civilians? Were civilians in the school, or the 306th Brigade? Who was in the school?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary school of Mehurici, or rather, the school building was mobilised for the requirements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, does that mean that in the extent to which the school building had been requisitioned by the 306th Brigade, that all the people inside it, inside the building, should have been, as far as logistics is concerned, supplied by the army?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, let's take this hypothetical question: At one given point, if there had been civilians on the premises requisitioned by the army, those civilians on the premises, how were they fed? Was it up to the army to feed them and to care for them and to cater to their needs? And if so, was it you on a logistical level who was the responsible person to do that?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had they been prisoners, then until they had been handed over to the higher organs of security authorised to take them over, you probably mean these civilians who were put up in the sports hall of the Mehurici school building from the Maline area, no, then it was not possible to do that. We as a logistics department did not have sufficient food to provide them, nor did we have the necessary medical equipment, nor did we treat them as prisoners. On the contrary. As far as I was able to understand at that point, the citizens of Maline were brought in to the school building of Mehurici and the sports hall of the primary school for security and safety reasons exclusively. And therefore, according to my information, we contacted the civilian organs of power and authority, the police, the civilian protection units, whose job it was to care for the refugees and displaced persons coming into the area. So as far as I remember, the command of the battalion, that's what the battalion command did. And the population was taken care of through the civilian protection. They were provided food as far as they were able. They were given medical assistance by the doctor in the area. And we, as a unit of the 1st Battalion, would lend a helping hand in ensuring that their stay was as secure as possible under those circumstances during that period, to avoid any problems. And as far as I understood it, we did not consider those prisoners in the prisoner category. We did not consider them to be prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So your answer to my question is that those -- as far as food for those people was concerned, and that is line 41 -- page 43, line 1, were taken over by the civilian authorities. So it was the civilian authorities whose job it was to bring them food. Right? Not you. You didn't have any responsibility with regard to supplying those people with food. Right?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall take note of your answers in that regard, with respect to supplying food to the civilians. Are there any additional questions? Follow-up questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Prosecution first. I forgot to turn to the Prosecution first. Any follow-up questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no follow-up questions. But may the witness please sign the map lying next to him and add today's date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What's the date today please? Would you tell me the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the 10th of November, 2004. Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution would like to tender the map. Well, let's have the map distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, we request this to be tendered into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. No objection. Mr. Registrar, may we have a number, just to see whether it's signed and dated. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be P936.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness once again be shown the decree law on the army, P243, please. Document P243, Article 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karic, in response to questions put to you by the President of the Trial Chamber, you said that the presidency would pass decrees, and that the parliament would later confirm them once it was able to meet. Do you remember whether this was one of those?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we confirmed the provisions or decrees, we would usually be given the number and date of the decree in question. That's what I remember. I'm not certain whether we confirmed this the first time we met, but I think it was rather quite a long time afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what I'm interested in is this: You spoke about the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, when it was gained, and the dissolution of Yugoslavia. Did you, as a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina, during that period of time know that on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, people were living who were not born in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Do you know that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, for example, there were quite a number of people who weren't actually born in Bosnia-Herzegovina, who were born elsewhere, in other parts of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was common knowledge. And I think I said yesterday that a lot of soldiers from Croatia, Slovenia were transferred to Bosnia-Herzegovina. And there were quite a number of what they called volunteers at the time who were from Serbia and Montenegro, for example, as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the people who weren't born in Bosnia-Herzegovina and who did not have permanent residence in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in keeping with the law on citizenship, were they considered to be foreign citizens, foreign nationals?

utterances.speaker: MUNIR KARIC [Resumed]
